subject: Post-call recap: Private/VPC options & networking constraints
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Mark Turner <mark.turner@cyberhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: Private/VPC options & networking constraints

Thanks again for your time today, Mark — really helpful conversation. Below is a quick recap of what we heard, and suggested next steps so we stay aligned. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of pain and drivers
- Data residency & regulatory drivers: CyberHealth needs PHI to remain within US-owned datacenters; customer data cannot leave the country.
- Network restrictions: Tight egress rules and an expected requirement for an air-gapped or very limited outbound connection for model updates/pulls.
- Performance & latency: Per-patient inference latency targets ~200ms p50 for triage workflows.
- Cost predictability: Finance wants a clear committed-cost model for the first 12 months to include reserved capacity.

What Redwood proposed on the call
- Private/VPC deployment (customer VPC) with optional on-prem package for air-gap scenarios.
- Dedicated capacity pools to meet latency and throughput SLOs; model pinning and local KV cache.
- KMS/HSM integration for key management and audit logs for compliance evidence.
- Network checklist and reference architecture attached for your team to review (redwood-private-arch.pdf).

Outstanding questions / clarifications we need from you
1) Target environment: Do you want a fully air-gapped on-prem install or a VPC deployment with tightly managed egress (allowed update windows)?
2) Approved datacenter/region list: Can you confirm the exact AWS accounts/regions or on-prem datacenters we should target?
3) Security evidence: Which artifacts are highest priority for your security review (SOC 2 Type II report, penetration test results, architecture diagrams)?
4) Timeline & procurement: You mentioned a Q2 2027 target — can you confirm procurement/PO timing and an internal stakeholder for the SOW?

Proposed next steps
- Camila/Marissa to send architecture doc + network checklist (attached) — ACTION: Marissa will follow with the network checklist.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with your network/security team next week to go through firewall rules and egress controls.
- Draft a provisional mutual action plan for procurement and security evidence.

Attachments: redwood-private-arch.pdf (architecture overview), network-checklist.xlsx (security/network checklist)

Thanks again — looking forward to continuing the conversation.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0132

From: Mark Turner <mark.turner@cyberhealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, procurement@cyberhealth.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 14:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Private/VPC options & networking constraints

Thanks, Camila — great summary. A few clarifications from our side after chatting internally: 

1) Environment: For Phase 1 we want a VPC deployment in our AWS accounts (us-west-2, us-east-1) with very restricted egress. Air-gap is a fallback if the security committee insists, but it will add time and cost.
2) Regions/accounts: Confirming us-west-2 and us-east-1; I'll share the specific account IDs in a separate secure ticket.
3) Evidence: SOC 2 Type II and penetration test results are mandatory. We will also need an architecture diagram that shows no persistent outbound connections from inference nodes except via your approved update gateway.
4) Latency: The 200ms p50 is a target; we'll run a short perf test during the technical deep-dive to validate.
5) Procurement/Timeline: We're aiming to start procurement discussions mid-Jan 2027 with a target pilot in Q2 2027. Procurement has asked for a ballpark committed-cost estimate for 12 months to include reserved capacity numbers.

Next steps from our side:
- I will open a ticket with our infra team and share account IDs.
- Procurement (procurement@cyberhealth.com) will expect a short commercial summary and an MSA redline.
- Security will share a short list of required artifacts — I'll loop them into the technical deep-dive invite.

Quick note: can Marissa share the network-checklist (spreadsheet) and a short doc that explains how the update gateway works and what outbound ports/addresses we'll need to allow? That will speed up our security review.

Thanks,
Mark Turner
Head of Infrastructure | CyberHealth Solutions
mark.turner@cyberhealth.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Mark Turner <mark.turner@cyberhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, procurement@cyberhealth.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Private/VPC options & networking constraints

Appreciate the fast follow, Mark — this is very helpful.

Marissa: looping you to share the network checklist + short note on the update gateway and allowed ports/addresses. Marissa, I put the checklist and the architecture overview in the attachments. Can you also add a 1-page summary that clearly states which ports are outbound and which AWS endpoints the update gateway will use?

Action items summary (owners):
- Marissa (Redwood): network-checklist.xlsx + update gateway note + perf test plan.
- Camila (Redwood): ballpark committed-cost estimate for 12 months + MSA template and commercial summary for procurement.
- Mark / CyberHealth: share AWS account IDs via secure ticket + security artifact priority list.

I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the technical deep-dive — proposed slots: Mon 11/16 10:00-11:00 PT or Tue 11/17 09:00-10:00 PT. Please confirm which works best.
